scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I live with my parents, and I pay them $200 a month, which they say is the market rate where we live. I've been living with them since I was pretty young, and most of the time, we get along. But I usually keep to myself, locking myself in my room to avoid them. Recently, there was a plumbing issue in my bathroom, so they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of this, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I guess that's why they were more around when I was playing Apex Legends on the couch. They went to Costco, and when they got home, my mom asked me to help bring in the groceries. I told her I'd do it in a minute, but I was too into my game to notice that they had to make several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get up, and when I said I'd do it in a minute, he grabbed the controller out of my hand and told me to get up now. That led to a big shouting match, and now they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which seems impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They're comparing me to him, which is really frustrating. I mean, I pay rent, so I thought that gave me the right to say no when they ask for help with groceries or yard work. But now they're threatening to kick me out, and I don't know what to do. Am I the asshole here? I guess I need to think about both sides. On one hand, I pay rent, and I thought that meant I could have some independence. But on the other hand, living with parents usually comes with some expectations of contributing to the household, even if it's just helping out with small things like bringing in groceries. Maybe I was too dismissive when they asked for help. I was in the middle of a game, but they had to make multiple trips, which could have been inconvenient or even frustrating for them. Grabbing the controller and telling me to get up now might have been a bit harsh, but maybe they felt like they had no choice after I kept putting them off. I also need to consider why they're so upset now. The remodel might have made it harder for them to avoid me, and the constant presence could have added stress to the situation. Plus, bringing up my brother seems like they're using him as an example of what I should be doing, which is unfair. But I also feel like I'm being treated like a child, even though I'm 33 and paying rent. I thought that by paying rent, I was contributing financially, which should give me some say in how I spend my time. Maybe I need to communicate better with them about my boundaries and expectations. Overall, I think both sides have some responsibility here. I should have been more considerate of their needs, especially since they had to remodel my section and are now around more. But they also shouldn't treat me like a child just because I'm living with them. It's a tough spot to be in, and I'm not sure if I'm entirely the asshole or if there's a middle ground.
